subject: Urgent: QuanticaEdge VPC throughput surge impacting inference — exec sync requested
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@quanticaedge.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: [QuanticaEdge] Sudden p95 jump + 503s across private VPC cluster

Karthik —

We started seeing a large spike in p95 latency and intermittent 503s across our private VPC deployment this morning (~09:30 PDT). Impact is user-facing: inference timeouts on customer-facing flows and increased queueing on our side. Attaching a quick metrics snapshot.

What we observe:
- p95 token latency increased from ~220ms to ~1.3s for our baseline seq=512 model
- 503s occurring in ~0.8% of requests, concentrated on a small subset of nodes
- Throughput per node dropped ~35% despite CPU/GPU util showing ~60% utilization

We need immediate triage and a plan for mitigation — QuanticaEdge execs are already asking for an explanation and timeline. Can your team triage and propose a short-term mitigation + a medium-term tuning plan?

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform Engineering
QuanticaEdge

Attachments: quanticaedge-kpi-snapshot-20280414.csv

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@quanticaedge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 16:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [QuanticaEdge] Sudden p95 jump + 503s across private VPC cluster

Elena —

Thanks for the snapshot and the early heads-up. We're looped in and prioritizing this. Quick plan:
1) I'll open a dedicated war room and get SRE/serving runtime on this immediately.
2) Short-term mitigations we'll validate within 2 hours: enable burst pool routing, lower max_batch_size for the affected model, temporarily move heavy background jobs off the cluster.
3) Medium-term: we'll run a KV cache warmup, validate kernel selection for the popular sequence length, and propose a targeted quantization profile if it helps throughput without quality loss.

Laura & Priyom — can you stand up the war room and pull logs/stack traces? Vivek/Mark — can you start a kernel/runtime diagnostic and look for signs of contention (NVLink/PCIe hot spots, CUDA kernel stalls, or model-thread scheduling anomalies)?

Elena, I'll propose a 30-min exec sync in 90 minutes to brief your leadership with a concrete mitigation timeline.

—Karthik
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: QuanticaEdge war room + initial artifacts

Team —

Stand-up notes from the initial triage (observed 16:50 PDT):
- Logs: multiple "KV cache miss" traces correlated with high latency spikes on 3 nodes (node ids attached).
- Runtime traces: decoder kernel average duration increased 2.8x on those nodes; queue length at the runtime queue mgr spiked.
- Node telemetry: GPU mem stable, but GPU compute utilization shows uneven distribution (some nodes at 92%, others at 40%).
- Recent changes: QuanticaEdge rolled a batch of model config changes this week (changed allowed_max_tokens and batch timeout) — Priyom, can you confirm config SHA/version?

Immediate actions we kicked off:
- Set model routing to favor healthy shards (reduces exposure to hot nodes) — done
- Reduced max_batch_size from 128->64 for the model serving customer traffic (should lower queuing latency) — testing now
- Prefetch/KV-cache warmup scheduled for the affected model on cold nodes (script attached)

Requests/asks:
- Vivek/Markus: prioritize kernel selection log collection and any recent GPU driver/firmware diffs.
- Priyom: share the model config version and the deployment manifest that QuanticaEdge applied this week.

I'll join the exec sync once we have a short mitigation update.

Laura
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rdw_playbook_quickpatch.txt

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 14 Apr 2028 18:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: QuanticaEdge war room + initial artifacts

Quick diagnostic summary (initial):
- Kernel mismatch on warmup: several shards are using a fallback matmul kernel that is suboptimal for the model's mixed precision profile; this explains the decoder spike.
- Observed NVLink bandwidth skew on three physical hosts — likely a transient topology scheduling issue after maintenance earlier in the week.
- There's a small regression in our continuous batching heuristic introduced in v1.9.4 that increases per-batch decode latency when batch timeouts are widened (matches QuanticaEdge's config change).

Short-term remedies applied (18:05 PDT):
- Forcing the preferred matmul kernel on affected nodes (immediate perf delta seen in canary)
- Reverting the widening of batch timeout in serving config for the QuanticaEdge model template
- Kicking an explicit KV-cache warmup job across affected shards

Expected impact: p95 should recover to ~300–400ms within 30–45 minutes for most traffic; we may still see residual 503s until queues drain.

I'll prepare a short doc with recommended medium-term tuning (kernel pinning policies, KV cache prewarm during deploys, and a conservative batching baseline) for the exec sync.

—Vivek
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@quanticaedge.com>, Mark Dawson <mark.dawson@quanticaedge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: [QuanticaEdge] Sudden p95 jump + 503s across private VPC cluster — exec sync follow-up

Elena / Mark —

Thank you for your patience. Quick summary of outcome and next steps from the war-room + exec sync:
- Short-term result: After kernel pinning, batch-timeout revert, and KV-cache warmup, observed p95 drop from ~1.3s to ~340ms and 503s dropped <0.15%. We will monitor through the day.
- Root causes identified: (1) suboptimal kernel selection post-deploy on a subset of hosts, (2) NVLink bandwidth skew on three hosts post-maintenance, and (3) a batching heuristic regression that amplified queuing under widened timeouts.

Recommended medium-term plan (timeline + owners):
- 0–7 days (SRE): Run full NVLink topology validation and remap instance placement where needed (Vivek)
- 1–2 weeks (Serving/runtime): Introduce kernel pinning policy for customer-critical models and extend our canary tests to surface kernel regressions (Markus)
- 1–3 weeks (Product/CS): Lock conservative batching defaults per workload class and add a pre-deploy KV-cache warmup step to the private deploy playbook (Priyom / Laura)

We created a HubSpot task and attached the playbook diffs and logs. I'll follow up tomorrow morning with a brief status note. If QuanticaEdge wants, we can schedule a dedicated post-mortem with their engineering execs.

Best,
Karthik
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
